cuts.item: The kind-manifest YAML system (Draft B §3: file format, match blocks, specificity resolution, loader, tie-break rules)
cuts.why: It is a plugin architecture for a community ecosystem of zero communities; v1's dozen lenses can be ordinary app code, and the elaborate loader denylist exists only to police an extension surface that does not have to be opened yet.

cuts.item: Charter kind packages (~/.gra/kinds cache, fetch by charter id+version, install-from-charter)
cuts.why: Distribution-and-caching infrastructure for third-party lenses nobody has written, defending a record that Draft B itself admits is already complete without them.

cuts.item: The `projection` mini-language (§1.2)
cuts.why: A query DSL whose specification is mostly the list of things it must never express; a hardcoded read-only panel is safe without a language.

cuts.item: Kind versioning and prospective-amendment rules (manifest `version`, Req 19.2 mapping)
cuts.why: Version discipline for manifest files that should not ship in v1 at all.

cuts.item: `degrades-to` declarations and the manifest-less-host fallback protocol
cuts.why: Fallback semantics matter only when lenses travel separately from the app; with builtin kinds only, every host renders identically and the record's own portability (C10) already covers the future.

cuts.item: The closed preconditions vocabulary (has-open-question, registrar-differs, charter-declares, disclosure-permits, ...)
cuts.why: A second, declarative implementation of lawfulness that will drift from grrp, when the drafts' own invariant — grrp refuses, stderr surfaced verbatim — already provides the single source of truth.

cuts.item: Bridge as a third action class
cuts.why: Draft C's S4 is correct: citing a hash is an artefact-picker parameter inside a real recording act, not a sibling class, and a free-standing 'cite' button produces transitions that exist only so a record exists (C1).

cuts.item: Administrative as a proposed fourth action class (Draft C S5's fix)
cuts.why: Instead of growing the taxonomy, collapse it: exactly two classes — actions that write the record through grrp (the 8 acts and the existing operations alike) and applicative actions test-proven to leave transitions/ byte-identical.

cuts.item: The twelve named occasion-kinds (lab meeting, seminar, journal club, supervision, whiteboard, conference, field trip, failed attempt, AI session, onboarding, ...)
cuts.why: They are one mechanism — trigger plus shared cited artefact — wearing different labels; specify the pattern once and let the trigger value be the label.

cuts.item: Occasion detection by hash+trigger+time-window clustering
cuts.why: Inference machinery for a grouping the graph already shows: the shared artefact node's citing edges ARE the occasion, no algorithm required.

cuts.item: Per-relation edge kinds (gra.edge.dispute and its eighteen siblings)
cuts.why: Nineteen kinds that differ only in a label and a match value; one connection presentation that renders the `relation` field covers all sixteen CiTO bindings and the three locals.

cuts.item: The material-kind catalogue beyond two (dataset, code release, manuscript draft, ethics letter, specimen sheet, instrument config, ...)
cuts.why: All of them are workflows over the same two node shapes — held artefact by state hash, external work by doi/arxiv/isbn/url — so the catalogue adds taxonomy, not capability.

cuts.item: Derived presentation edges (same-source, same-occasion, chronological adjacency)
cuts.why: Computed overlays that carry fresh C6 guard obligations in order to duplicate what the shared node's ordinary edges already display.

cuts.item: Five separate record-facet component types (identity, details, bearing, material, provenance)
cuts.why: Five tabs over one small signed YAML; a single read-only record panel that renders the whole payload is simpler and harder to get wrong.

cuts.item: `endpoints` as an edge-family component
cuts.why: It is `bearing` (parents/children) renamed.

cuts.item: `note` and `form` component types
cuts.why: A named markdown file and a schema'd YAML file are both just files in the workspace folder the workspace component already provides.

cuts.item: `commitments` component
cuts.why: A read-only re-display of release_at and embargo dates that the disclosure panel already shows.

cuts.item: The composition algebra (universal set ∪ family defaults ∪ kind list, id-conflict resolution, builtins-win-actions/charters-win-components tie-breaks)
cuts.why: With four components and a handful of hardcoded kinds, each kind's panel list is a short literal list — and inheritance rules are exactly how a calendar ends up on a dispute edge (Draft C's S9).

cuts.item: `join-meeting` as a specified action
cuts.why: It is a hyperlink stored in a calendar entry; elevating it to named action machinery manufactures the presence-logging trap that S3 then has to defuse.

cuts.item: Occasion badges and any per-node count decorations on the canvas
cuts.why: Draft C's S8 is right that badges across a canvas are comparison by juxtaposition, so counts live only inside the one selected item's panel and no badge component exists at all.

cuts.item: Draft A's workspace-content enumerations (PDF annotation layer, onboarding tour bookmarks, reviewer-response drafting table, per-node task checklist)
cuts.why: The workspace is an ordinary folder; enumerating its possible contents in a specification is documentation cosplaying as design surface.

cuts.item: The 47-ruling gauntlet as normative spec text
cuts.why: Keep it as review record, but a spec that implementers must diff against 47 numbered rulings will be skimmed, not obeyed — the spec itself carries a one-page constitutive refusal table.

kernel: V1 commits to seven things and nothing else. (1) grrp is the sole record-writer: every record-writing action — the 8 acts plus the existing administrative operations — is a thin form over exactly one grrp invocation, with artefact citation as a picker parameter of the act, and grrp's refusal surfaced verbatim; no declarative precondition layer, no UI-constructed skeletons. (2) Exactly two action classes: grrp-writing and applicative, with the existing upload test generalised so every applicative action provably leaves transitions/ byte-identical. (3) Three node presentations, hardcoded in app code: transition (labeled by its act, protocol term always one gesture away), held artefact (state hash), and external work (doi/arxiv/isbn/url, rendering fully offline). (4) Two edge presentations: structural parent edges as bare facts — no identity, no components, and the written-down rule that a bad link is contested by challenging the child transition whose signed payload carries it — and connection transitions, drawn as edges, openable as nodes. (5) Exactly four components, one per layer: a read-only record panel (the whole signed payload), a disclosure panel (sidecar, widen-only, grounds and release_at included), a workspace folder on every node and every connection (mutable, never bundled — the brief's one universal), and a calendar entry (local plane, never exported, schema containing no people fields, granted only to meeting occasions). (6) Occasions are derived and never creatable: a shared cited artefact is the occasion node, its citing edges are the gathering, and no view ever unions their performers into a roster. (7) A one-page constitutive refusal table in the spec: no person or project nodes, no attendance anywhere in any layer, no scalars/weights/rankings/progress/streaks, no merge and the word never appears, no edit/delete/unpublish, no mark-resolved, no per-performer views, counts only inside the single selected item's panel. Everything cut above — manifests, charter kind packages, projections, occasion and relation catalogues — is deferred until a second real community exists, and deferring it is safe precisely because kinds are lenses that never touch the record: any future lens can reread everything v1 writes.
